items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: And I had a date coming up where I was playing with his band that he told me about

ctx.x: Now yeah. The — I’m trying to remember when the first one hit, it was a device called a sampler, which was really not a synthesizer, it has nothing to do with the tradition of or

the lore or the background or the genealogy of the synthesizer, which is an electronic instrument. It goes back to the stuff that Robert Moog built years ago, which was designed to make unique electronic sounds. The sampler, the only similarity is it’s just controlled by a keyboard. It essentially records instruments, records them very well into computer memory, and you configure it to respond properly. You play a middle C on a keyboard, a recording of a trumpet or whatever, or a violin section playing middle C.…
Right. You could probably have a museum someday.
